summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY command, which requires Enterprise Edition or higher. It explains the syntax (CREATE [OR REPLACE] ROW ACCESS POLICY [IF NOT EXISTS] with an AS signature, RETURNS BOOLEAN body and optional COMMENT), the required and optional parameters, the schema-level CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY privilege, and usage notes such as a column cannot appear in both a masking policy and a row access policy signature. Three examples show policies based on current_role() checks and a subquery against a salesmanagerregions mapping table.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY command, covering syntax, parameters, privileges, usage notes and examples.
key_facts: The CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY feature requires Enterprise Edition (or higher) in Snowflake.
Creating a row access policy creates it in the current or specified schema, or replaces an existing row access policy.
After creating a row access policy, the policy must be added to a table using an ALTER command.
The syntax is CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] ROW ACCESS POLICY [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <name> AS ( <arg_name> <arg_type> [ , ... ] ) RETURNS BOOLEAN -> <body> [ COMMENT = '<string_literal>' ].
The name identifier must be unique for the schema, must start with an alphabetic character, and identifiers in double quotes are case-sensitive.
A row access policy must evaluate to true or false, and the body can be any boolean-valued SQL expression.
The optional COMMENT parameter has a default of no value.
The role executing the command must have the CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY privilege on the schema, plus USAGE on the parent database and schema.
A given table or view column cannot be specified in both a masking policy signature and a row access policy signature at the same time.
CREATE OR REPLACE statements are atomic: the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.
Example rap_it returns true only when current_role() is 'it_admin'.
Example rap_sales_manager_regions_1 allows the 'sales_executive_role' role, or a sales_manager role whose region appears in the salesmanagerregions mapping table.
Example rap_test2 has the signature (n number, v varchar) and returns true, granting access to all rows.
